result.target_summary: Fiscal year 2024 was a 53-week year compared to the 52-week fiscal year 2023, with the additional week in the first quarter resulting in higher net revenue, gross margin dollars, and operating expenses for the period.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosure (D036) defines the fiscal year convention (52/53 weeks ending near Oct 31) and states that 2023 was a 52-week year. The 2024 filing splits this topic: D043 defines the general convention (similar to 2023 D036), while D003 specifically discusses the 2024 vs 2023 comparison (53-week vs 52-week) and the impact of the extra week. D003 contains specific comparative data not present in D043, and D043 contains the general policy definition present in D036. Both are needed to cover the fiscal year presentation topic completely.

comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue increased to 49% in 2024 from 46% in 2023. This increase was primarily driven by a favorable shift in revenue mix towards higher Data Center and Client revenues, as well as lower Gaming revenue, which was partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss financial performance drivers for fiscal year 2024, but differ in their primary focus on operating metrics. Broadcom attributes higher gross margin dollars and operating expenses in 2024 to the structural impact of a 53-week fiscal year, noting the additional week in the first quarter. In contrast, AMD attributes its improved gross margin percentage (49% vs 46%) primarily to a favorable shift in revenue mix towards higher Data Center and Client revenues, rather than calendar week variations.

sentences.text: The additional week in the first quarter of fiscal year 2024 resulted in higher net revenue, gross margin dollars, research and development expense, and selling general and administrative expense for fiscal year 2024, compared to the corresponding prior year fiscal period.
Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue was 49% in 2024 compared to 46% in 2023.
The increase in gross margin was due to a favorable shift in revenue mix of higher Data Center and Client revenues, lower Gaming revenue, partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.

comparisons.peer_summary: Amortization of acquisition-related intangibles was $2.4 billion for 2024, a decrease of 15% from $2.8 billion in 2023, primarily due to certain intangibles being fully amortized in the prior fiscal year.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address expense composition changes in 2024. Broadcom explicitly lists research and development and selling, general, and administrative expenses as being higher due to the extra week in the fiscal year. AMD separately discusses a significant decrease in amortization of acquisition-related intangibles ($2.4 billion, down 15% from 2023) driven by certain intangibles being fully amortized, representing a different type of expense driver unrelated to the fiscal calendar duration.

sentences.text: The additional week in the first quarter of fiscal year 2024 resulted in higher net revenue, gross margin dollars, research and development expense, and selling general and administrative expense for fiscal year 2024, compared to the corresponding prior year fiscal period.
Amortization of acquisition-related intangibles of $2.4 billion for 2024 decreased by $417 million, or 15%, compared to $2.8 billion in 2023.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2024 Impairment and Depreciation Charges Impacting Gross Margin
comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin decreased by $4.4 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by $3.3 billion in impairment and accelerated depreciation charges related to manufacturing assets exceeding capacity for the Intel 7 process node, as well as $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss the financial impact on gross margin and operating expenses in 2024, but cite opposite directions and causes. Broadcom reports higher gross margin dollars for fiscal year 2024 compared to the prior year period, attributing this increase to the additional week in a 53-week fiscal year. Conversely, Intel reports a decrease in consolidated gross margin of $4.4 billion (20%) in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by $3.3 billion in impairment and accelerated depreciation charges rather than calendar effects.

sentences.text: The additional week in the first quarter of fiscal year 2024 resulted in higher net revenue, gross margin dollars, research and development expense, and selling general and administrative expense for fiscal year 2024, compared to the corresponding prior year fiscal period.
Our consolidated gross margin in 2024 decreased by $4.4 billion, or 20%, compared to 2023 due primarily to higher 2024 impairment charges and accelerated depreciation.

Upon completing an asset re-use assessment, we impaired certain construction-in-progress assets and accelerated depreciation for certain in-use manufacturing assets that resulted in $3.3 billion of charges in 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin improved to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, aided by increased average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, despite the prior year's inventory write-downs and lower costs from selling previously written-down inventory in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures describe the trajectory of gross margin performance in 2024 relative to 2023. Broadcom notes that the 53-week fiscal year 2024 resulted in higher gross margin dollars compared to the 52-week prior year. Micron highlights a dramatic recovery in gross margin percentage, improving to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, driven by increased average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, contrasting Broadcom's calendar-based growth with Micron's price/cost-driven turnaround.

sentences.text: The additional week in the first quarter of fiscal year 2024 resulted in higher net revenue, gross margin dollars, research and development expense, and selling general and administrative expense for fiscal year 2024, compared to the corresponding prior year fiscal period.

Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).

comparisons.peer_summary: SG&A expenses increased 23% in 2024 compared to 2023 primarily due to higher employee compensation, whereas 2023 expenses were 14% lower than 2022 due to decreases in compensation, legal fees, advertising, and professional services.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the trend in operating expenses, specifically SG&A or general corporate costs. Broadcom identifies that the additional week in the 53-week fiscal 2024 resulted in higher selling, general, and administrative expenses compared to the prior year. Micron reports a 23% increase in SG&A expenses in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by higher employee compensation, which is a distinct driver from Broadcom's calendar-induced increase.

sentences.text: The additional week in the first quarter of fiscal year 2024 resulted in higher net revenue, gross margin dollars, research and development expense, and selling general and administrative expense for fiscal year 2024, compared to the corresponding prior year fiscal period.
Selling, General, and Administrative: SG&A expenses for 2024 increased 23% as compared to 2023 primarily due to an increase in employee compensation.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fiscal 2024 gross margin performance and drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Overall gross margin increased to 72.7% in fiscal year 2024 from 56.9% in fiscal year 2023, primarily driven by 217% growth in Data Center revenue and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures analyze gross margin performance in fiscal 2024 but attribute the results to different factors. Broadcom attributes higher gross margin dollars to the 53-week fiscal calendar adding an extra week of revenue. NVIDIA attributes a significant increase in overall gross margin percentage (from 56.9% to 72.7%) to strong Data Center revenue growth of 217% and lower net inventory provisions, indicating organic growth drivers rather than calendar duration effects.

sentences.text: The additional week in the first quarter of fiscal year 2024 resulted in higher net revenue, gross margin dollars, research and development expense, and selling general and administrative expense for fiscal year 2024, compared to the corresponding prior year fiscal period.
Our overall gross margin increased to 72.7% in fiscal year 2024 from 56.9% in fiscal year 2023.
The year over year increase was primarily due to strong Data Center revenue growth of 217% and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
